notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Wedge-shaped bollards with an orange rectangular reflector on the front and a white one on the back; a thin version exists too.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Square concrete poles, often with a diagonal support beam; seen occasionally in Estonia and rarely in Latvia.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole tops with short horizontal rods holding insulators, sometimes in a trident layout; common across post-Soviet states.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: White chevrons with red arrows; small single ones have a red outline. Estonia, Russia and Ukraine use the reverse colours.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The L-shaped blue kilometre marker stands at about 45 degrees to the road.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning and speed signs have a relatively thin red border with a thin white outline.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Normal A-type guardrails with orange reflectors. Estonia has none; Latvia uses red or white.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Pedestrian sign has three stripes and a simple figure, same as Russia and Ukraine; Estonia's is more detailed.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Bus stop sign shows a bus with four windows, like Estonia; Latvia's has five.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Hooked vowels Ą Ę Į Ų, dotted Ė, and a plain Y are unique among the Baltic languages.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The word for street is "gatvė", often shortened to g. Many place names end in -ai.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Light-coloured brick buildings with steep corrugated metal roofs; wood is less common than in Estonia.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The historic flag with a mounted knight on dark red is sometimes flown on buildings.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Less forest than the other Baltic states, so scenery looks more open and farmed. Use with caution.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 coverage shows odd small random blurs, often on direction signs; also common in Russia's Kaliningrad.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Overall flat, no hills above 300 m; the biggest hills are in the southeast, some in the central west.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Metal tags on poles are mostly found in the east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A long sand-dune spit with a north-south road, windswept pines and red wooden Scandinavian-style houses.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Rarely, signs with Polish added appear in a small area in the southeast.
